interview_parallel: Razorpay / Cred backend senior round — refactor a hot-path rate limiter that cannot be unit-tested and silently allows bursts; make it deterministic and correct without changing the public allow() contract
acceptance_criteria: `TokenBucket` is exported as a constructor/class and accepts an injectable `now` clock
Refill is incremental and capped at `capacity` — a one-second pause does NOT restore the bucket to full unless refillPerSec × elapsed reaches capacity
`tryRemove(n)` refills first, then removes n tokens if available (true) else returns false
`allow()` is preserved as a module-level wrapper and still exported
Both visible tests pass against the refactored code

visible_tests.name: token_bucket_is_exported_and_injectable
visible_tests.command: node -e "const m = require('./rateLimiter'); if (typeof m.TokenBucket !== 'function') { console.error('TokenBucket not exported'); process.exit(1); } const b = new m.TokenBucket({ capacity: 2, refillPerSec: 1, now: () => 0 }); if (typeof b.tryRemove !== 'function') { console.error('no tryRemove'); process.exit(1); } console.log('PASS');"

visible_tests.name: incremental_refill_bounds_sustained_rate
visible_tests.command: node -e "const { TokenBucket } = require('./rateLimiter'); let t = 0; const b = new TokenBucket({ capacity: 2, refillPerSec: 1, now: () => t }); const seq = []; seq.push(b.tryRemove()); seq.push(b.tryRemove()); seq.push(b.tryRemove()); t = 1000; seq.push(b.tryRemove()); seq.push(b.tryRemove()); const expected = [true, true, false, true, false]; if (JSON.stringify(seq) !== JSON.stringify(expected)) { console.error('got ' + JSON.stringify(seq)); process.exit(1); } console.log('PASS');"

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Refactors into a TokenBucket class but preserves the original reset-to-full refill (`this.tokens = this.capacity`) instead of incremental accrual — the sustained-rate test fails because a one-second pause on a capacity-2 / 1-per-sec bucket restores 2 tokens instead of 1.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: The learner is asked to "extract a class", so the model faithfully copies the existing (buggy) body into a method without questioning the refill math. Preserving behaviour is usually the safe refactoring instinct — here the behaviour itself was the bug.
detection_signals: incremental_refill_bounds_sustained_rate returns [true,true,false,true,true] (5th call true) instead of [...,false]
The refill method assigns capacity directly rather than adding elapsed × refillPerSec

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Keeps reading `Date.now()` inside the class instead of accepting an injectable `now`, so the deterministic test that drives a fake clock cannot control time and the bucket never observes the simulated 1-second jump.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: Dependency-injecting the clock is a testing-specific idiom; without an explicit instruction the model reaches for the familiar `Date.now()` it saw in the starter.
detection_signals: token_bucket_is_exported_and_injectable constructs with `now: () => 0` but the bucket ignores it
No `now` parameter in the constructor signature

seeded_mistakes.bug_description: Extracts TokenBucket but forgets to keep the module-level `allow()` wrapper (or stops exporting it), breaking every existing caller that imports `{ allow }`.
seeded_mistakes.why_compass_might_suggest_it: Once the class exists the old free function looks redundant, so the model deletes it — not realising callers still depend on the original named export.

rubric_anchors.check: `TokenBucket` is a top-level exported class taking `{ capacity, refillPerSec, now }` with an injectable clock defaulting to `() => Date.now()`
Refill is incremental and capped (elapsed × refillPerSec, min capacity) — both visible tests pass, proving a one-second pause does not restore full capacity
`allow()` is preserved as a module-level wrapper over a default bucket and both `TokenBucket` and `allow` are exported
Learner's prompt explicitly named the injectable clock AND incremental-refill requirement — not just "make it a class"

good_prompts_look_like: States "inject the clock as a `now()` function so time can be faked in tests" rather than "make it testable"
Specifies "refill incrementally: add elapsed × refillPerSec, capped at capacity — do not reset to full"
Requires that the existing `allow()` export be preserved so no caller breaks
common_verification_traps: Testing only that tokens deplete (the happy path) and never advancing the clock — the reset-to-full bug only shows after time passes
Asserting the class exists without driving it with a fake clock — the Date.now() version "works" but is not deterministic
